Prior fires on this module attacked: the flagship KPI's generalization via a 10-molecule live-RDKit-FFI probe (BDMA/EMI-24/DICY/ethers/aspartic-esters/sulfones/hindered-aromatics -- SURVIVED); the Macosko-Miller H2 sol-latitude direction rule via non-ideal reactivity-ratio Monte Carlo (SURVIVED); the fitted logistic model via honest LOOCV+conformal (parsimony-conformal, SURVIVED/noninferior); the Flory-Stockmayer gelation rule (SURVIVED); fact-provenance invariance (SURVIVED, 39/39). This fire escalates past the live-runtime-domain-probe-v1 hostile-null set by targeting a specific structural gap that set never covered: a real cure-accelerator chemotype with genuine non-aromatic N-H that neither of the two previously-tested accelerator/catalyst nulls (BDMA, EMI-24) exercised.

input_artifacts.bridge_cc_reference: amphora-rdkit-ffi/src/bridge.cc::count_reactive_amine_hydrogens (lines ~66-89: excludes only is_carbonyl_carbon / is_sulfonyl_sulfur neighbors; no is_amidine/is_guanidine neighbor check exists)

method: Invoked the REAL production RDKit C++ FFI (amphora_rdkit_ffi::molecule_facts, pinned RDKit 2026.03.2, exact_version_match=true recorded in toolkit_provenance) -- not a Python re-derivation -- via a small Rust harness on two real, named, CAS-identified, industrially dominant guanidine-class cure accelerators: 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG, CAS 102-06-7) and N,N'-di-o-tolylguanidine (DOTG, CAS 97-39-2). Both are documented exclusively as catalytic accelerators (DPG/DOTG: dominant rubber-vulcanization secondary accelerators, boosting thiazole/thiuram/sulfenamide primary accelerators; DPG additionally documented in US Patent 9,238,706 'Use of guanidine derivatives as curing accelerators for epoxy resins' as a guanidine-class epoxy curing ACCELERATOR), never as a stoichiometric amine-hydrogen-consuming hardener in either industry. Verified computed molecular formula/MW against independently published values (DPG: C13H13N3, MW 211.26/211.268 observed; DOTG: C15H17N3, MW 239.32/239.322 observed) before scoring, confirming the SMILES correctly encode the named compounds. Pre-registered refute criterion: attack fires if either probe's observed_role is 'hardener' rather than 'out_of_domain' (the fail-closed behavior the module's own BDMA/EMI-24 probes established as correct for real accelerator/catalyst molecules).
objective: Test whether amphora-rdkit-ffi/src/bridge.cc::count_reactive_amine_hydrogens (the live production RDKit C++ logic the role-ranker Rust runtime consumes byte-identically) and the module's deterministic role rule (has_oxirane=false & reactive_amine_hydrogen_count>0 => hardener) correctly fail closed on real, named, commercially dominant, coating/rubber-relevant cure ACCELERATOR molecules whose N-H is guanidine-type: neither absent (unlike BDMA, a tertiary amine with zero N-H) nor aromatic (unlike EMI-24, whose ring N-H is pyrrole-type). count_reactive_amine_hydrogens only excludes a nitrogen's hydrogens when its direct neighbor carbon is carbonyl/thiocarbonyl (is_carbonyl_carbon, C=O or C=S) or when a neighbor sulfur is sulfonyl (is_sulfonyl_sulfur); a guanidine/amidine neighbor carbon (C=N) triggers neither exclusion, so its N-H count as 'reactive amine hydrogen' with no structural signal that the molecule's real formulation role is catalytic, not stoichiometric.
pre_registered_refute_criterion: Attack fires (REFUTED) iff either probe's observed_role != 'out_of_domain'. Both probes (dpg-diphenylguanidine-accelerator, dotg-di-o-tolylguanidine-accelerator) observed_role == 'hardener'. Criterion met on 2/2 probes.

US Patent 9,238,706, 'Use of guanidine derivatives as curing accelerators for epoxy resins' -- documents guanidine-class compounds (the DPG/DOTG chemotype) functioning as epoxy cure ACCELERATORS, not stoichiometric hardeners.
N,N'-di-o-tolylguanidine (DOTG), CAS 97-39-2, C15H17N3, MW 239.32 -- rubber vulcanization accelerator, more active analog of DPG, not a curing agent (widely documented industrial/CAS reference data).

probes.citation: 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG, CAS 102-06-7), formula C13H13N3, MW 211.26. The dominant medium-speed secondary accelerator for natural/synthetic rubber vulcanization (boosts thiazole/thiuram/sulfenamide primary accelerators), and separately documented in the epoxy-curing patent literature specifically as a guanidine-class curing ACCELERATOR (US Patent 9,238,706, 'Use of guanidine derivatives as curing accelerators for epoxy resins') -- never described as a stoichiometric amine-hydrogen-consuming hardener in either industry.
probes.note: hostile-null: a real, commercially dominant catalytic accelerator with THREE non-aromatic, non-charged N-H hydrogens (two anilide-type N-H plus one guanidine =N-H), none adjacent to a carbonyl (C=O/C=S) or sulfonyl carbon/sulfur. The module's own prior hostile-null probes (BDMA: zero N-H; EMI-24: aromatic ring N-H) were both excluded by orthogonal mechanisms and never stress-tested count_reactive_amine_hydrogens' actual exclusion predicate, which checks only for a C=O/C=S (is_carbonyl_carbon) or -SO2- (is_sulfonyl_sulfur) neighbor -- never a C=N (guanidine/amidine) neighbor.

probes.citation: N,N'-di-o-tolylguanidine (DOTG, CAS 97-39-2), formula C15H17N3, MW 239.32. A more active structural analog of DPG, documented exclusively as a rubber vulcanization accelerator/booster for thiazole-thiuram-sulfonamide systems -- not a curing agent -- included as a second, independent instance of the same guanidine-accelerator chemotype to show the gap is not a one-off artifact of the DPG structure.
probes.note: second independent instance of the same non-aromatic guanidine N-H chemotype as dpg-diphenylguanidine-accelerator, ortho-methyl substituted; tests that the gap generalizes across substitution and is not specific to the unsubstituted phenyl ring.

recommended_followups: Extend bridge.cc's is_carbonyl_carbon-style exclusion (or add a parallel is_amidine_or_guanidine_carbon check) so a nitrogen whose neighbor carbon bears a C=N double bond to another nitrogen is treated the same way as the existing C=O/C=S exclusion, OR add an explicit accelerator/catalyst denylist gate ahead of the has_reactive_amine_hydrogen role rule.

Add DPG- and DOTG-class guanidine accelerators to the module's own 39-record known-answer fixture and to role-live-runtime-domain-probe-v1's hostile-null probe set, alongside BDMA and EMI-24, so this chemotype is regression-guarded going forward.

scope_note: Does not assert a single 'correct' reactive_amine_hydrogen_count for guanidine N-H in the AHEW/quantitative sense (that mechanistic question, raised for the amine-class active-N-H rule in a sibling module, is out of scope here). The refutation is scoped to the CATEGORICAL role_fit classification: whether a real, documented, non-stoichiometric cure accelerator is silently promoted to 'hardener' stoichiometric status, which is sufficient to falsify the flagship KPI's implicit domain-generalization claim regardless of the unsettled guanidine-nucleophilicity mechanism question.
why: Both real, named, CAS-verified guanidine-class cure accelerators (DPG, DOTG) are classified 'hardener' by the live production runtime (reactive_amine_hydrogen_count=3, has_oxirane=false) when their documented real-world formulation role in both the rubber and epoxy literatures is catalytic accelerator, not stoichiometric hardener. This is the exact failure mode the module's own prior hostile-null probes (BDMA, EMI-24) were designed to catch and correctly caught -- but via orthogonal exclusion paths (zero N-H; aromatic N-H) that do not cover the guanidine/amidine C=N chemotype. The flagship KPI's structural_inference_agreement_rate=1.0 and the live-runtime-domain-probe-v1 SURVIVED verdict do not bound this failure mode because neither the self-authored fixture nor the prior probe set contains a non-aromatic, non-charged, non-carbonyl-adjacent accelerator N-H case.
